model.description: MODEL_JUDGE - the identity judgement of the nightly canonicalisation round (ruling Q1). This is the one place in the hive that deliberately carries the STRONGEST model available, not the cheapest that works: the verdict is written into the store as an alias and every later read consumes it. The default is a top-tier placeholder rather than an empty string, because an unconfigured judge would silently skip the canonicalisation round every night; set it explicitly at rollout.

reasoning_effort.description: Explicit reasoning effort (MEMORY_REASONING_JUDGE) - never inherit the provider default

description.purpose: Judges IDENTITY for the nightly canonicalisation round (0.2.0 P5, rulings Q1/Q3/Q5): which predicate keys name the same relation, and which entity candidate pairs are the same person, place or thing. It is the persisting twin of the extractor - the extractor keeps a new turn on the axes that exist, this one repairs the axes that already fell apart. Top tier on purpose, once a night, never per turn.
description.use_when: Called by dream-glue once per consolidation run, after the dreamer's verdicts are parked and before the supersession arithmetic, with the predicate inventory and the fuzzy entity candidates in one payload.
description.not_in_scope: No store access and no effect of its own: dream-glue turns the verdict into set_alias / reject_pair / canonicalize, all additive and revertible. It never deletes, never rewrites a written value, and never judges supersession (that is arithmetic). It also never invents a name - every value it returns has to come from the payload.
description.emits_meaning: messages[]: one assistant turn holding the judgement JSON {predicates:[{alias,canonical}], entities:[{alias,canonical}], different:[{dimension,left,right}]}. hop.finish_reason='error' makes dream-glue skip the round and continue with the rest of the run instead of leaving it hanging.
description.consumes_meaning: system.instructions.text: the judgement contract, handed over by dream-glue (an llm cell has no params.system - the prompt travels in the message). messages[]: the predicate inventory with the subjects each key is used on, plus the candidate entity pairs with the facts of both sides.
examples: predicates 'Lieblingseditor' and 'favorite_editor', both used on subject 'user' -> {"predicates":[{"alias":"Lieblingseditor","canonical":"favorite_editor"}]}
entity pair ('ashford','ashfrd'), one with two facts and one with a single typo-shaped fact -> {"entities":[{"alias":"elvse","canonical":"elvese"}]}
entity pair ('robin','robyn'), each with its own birthday fact -> {"different":[{"dimension":"subject","left":"robin","right":"robyn"}]} - remembered, so the pair is never proposed again
